newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha steady, but demand stays relaxed.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha steady, but demand stays relaxed.

text.p: European spot naphtha prices were steady in quiet trade on Wednesday underpinned by firmer futures but with physical demand staying relaxed, traders said.

Swaps were stable, picking up the bullish gasoline undertone after Tuesday's API report showed "implied demand" for U.S. gasoline at a record 8.76 million barrels per day, in contrast to an EIA report showing "underwhelming demand" this year.
However, physical demand for heavier N+A material to make gasoline remained thin.
NWE full range cargoes were notionally assessed around $173/$176 a tonne cif.
An 8kt Dow spec parcel reported was traded on Tuesday at around $174 for delivery by May 11.
Trade in the Mediterranean remained dull but prices held steady around $173 a tonne cif Med with few stems showing and some ongoing arbitrage buying interest.
